angle_name: Landau–Gonek zero-pair resolvent decomposition at the K=√x symmetry point
mechanism: Pass from R = π−Li to the ψ-normalization by one Abel summation in d (legitimate since log(x/d) ∈ [½log x, log x] on the whole support d ≤ K; cost ≪ √x·polylog), reducing the target to S_ψ = Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)(ψ(⌊x/d⌋) − x/d). Apply the truncated explicit formula at the PINNED point x with height T = x: summing the per-term truncation error O((x/d)log²x / T) over d ≤ K costs only O(log³x), so pointwise validity at the synchronized x is free — no L² averaging is ever invoked. This yields S_ψ = −Σ_{|γ|≤T} (x^ρ/ρ)·F_K(ρ) + O(polylog), where F_K(s) = Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)d^{−s} is the truncated Dirichlet series of 1/ζ. Evaluate F_K at the zero ρ itself by truncated Perron: because ζ(ρ)=0, the integrand K^w/(w·ζ(ρ+w)) has a double pole at w=0 contributing (log K + c_ρ)/ζ'(ρ) (simple zeros), plus off-diagonal residues Σ_{ρ'≠ρ} K^{ρ'−ρ}/((ρ'−ρ)ζ'(ρ')). Substituting splits S_ψ = D + O_off: the diagonal D = −(log K)·Σ_ρ x^ρ/(ρζ'(ρ)) is EXACTLY the classical zero-sum for M(x), i.e., D ≈ −M(x)·log K — consistent with the exact identity Σ_{d≤x} μ(d)ψ(x/d) = −Σ_{n≤x} μ(n)log n (from μ∗Λ = −μ·log), so the RH-equivalent content of the target is quarantined in one identified term. The off-diagonal is where the lens earns its keep: x^ρ·K^{ρ'−ρ} = x^{(ρ+ρ')/2} at K = √x — the canonical choice y ≍ √x is precisely the symmetry point at which every zero-pair contributes amplitude x^{(β+β')/2} with phase (γ+γ')/2·log x, weighted 1/(ρ(ρ'−ρ)ζ'(ρ')). So the μ×R sign interaction is transported, without any splitting over d, into a bilinear zero-pair sum governed by three statistics: the phases x^{i(γ+γ')/2}, the discrete moments J_{−1}(T) = Σ_{γ≤T}|ζ'(ρ)|^{−2}, and small-gap behavior of |ρ−ρ'|. On RH these are exactly the objects of Nathan Ng's conditional theory of M(x) (UNVERIFIED literature claim: Ng 2004, assuming RH and J_{−1}(T) ≪ T, controls M(x) to √x·polylog); the Abel sum is a new two-zero generalization of that framework, with the ρ'=ρ̄ conjugate-pair subdiagonal (phase-free, size Σ_γ x^β/(γ²|ζ'(ρ)|²)-type) handled by the same moment hypothesis. Nothing in the argument bounds Σ M(d)² or recombines over d by Cauchy–Schwarz; the recombination happens over zero pairs, where the cancellation structure is Landau/Gonek-type and not subject to the F(σ) ≥ 1/2 + σ/2 expansion.
new_leverage: Three things not present in the declared obstacle coordinates: (1) the explicit formula is a pointwise identity at the pinned, synchronized x (truncation error polylog at T = x) — this lens natively evades the pinned-vs-averaged wall rather than fighting it; (2) the Perron evaluation of F_K(ρ) at a zero of ζ converts the d-sum into per-zero data (log K)/ζ'(ρ) plus zero-pair resolvents, so the diagonal is exactly −M(x)log K: the circular part of the target is isolated into one named term instead of contaminating every estimate; (3) at K = √x the off-diagonal phases symmetrize to x^{i(γ+γ')/2}, making the residual difficulty precisely a two-zero discrete moment problem (J_{−1} plus gap statistics) — a known, partially developed technology (Gonek, Hejhal, Ng — UNVERIFIED capability claims) rather than an unstructured bilinear wall. Additionally, the multiplicative-shift autocorrelations that appear if one instead expands via Landau's formula (terms μ(d)μ(dp)Λ-type) are computable, unlike additive Chowla correlations — a reserve identity the sieve-coordinate approaches cannot see.
target_estimate: With x ∈ ℕ, y = ⌊√x⌋, K = ⌊x/(y+1)⌋ (so K ≍ √x): |Σ_{d=1}^{K} μ(d)·(π(⌊x/d⌋) − Li(⌊x/d⌋))| ≪_ε x^{1/2+ε}, uniformly in x (Lean object: primeSieveMoebiusDiscrepancySum y x, RHLean/Analysis/PrimeSieveAbelIdentity.lean; boundary term M(K)·(π(y)−Li(y)) separately self-consistent per packet). Losses budgeted by the mechanism: (a) π−Li → (ψ−id)/log transfer via second Abel summation in d: ≪ √x·log x; (b) explicit-formula truncation at T = x summed over d ≤ K: O(log³x); (c) Perron evaluation of F_K(ρ): per-zero horizontal-contour and near-zero-cluster errors, which must be summable against x^β/|ρ| — this is the step where all remaining difficulty concentrates and where the conditional hypotheses (RH, simple zeros, J_{−1}(T) ≪ T·(log T)^{O(1)}, mild gap-moment) enter. Conditional deliverable form: S ≪ √x·(log x)^{C}.

obstacle_positions.F_closure: Exits the class by construction: the only recombination is over zero pairs (ρ,ρ'), never over d; no step inputs Σ_{d≤D}M(d)² and no Cauchy–Schwarz/Hölder/triangle split over d occurs — the μ×R interaction survives verbatim as x^{i(γ+γ')/2} phases with 1/ζ' weights. Acknowledged residual risk: if at any point I am forced to Cauchy–Schwarz over ZEROS with trivial |F_K| bounds, the bound collapses back to exactly the trivial scale x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}) (I checked: x^β·K^{1−β} = x^{(1+β)/2} reproduces the triangle bound term-for-term), i.e., an analog closure exists in zero coordinates and must be avoided the same way.
obstacle_positions.fiber_growth: Not engaged: no pair→modulus transfer, no reduced-denominator coordinates, no conductors. The structural analog of large fibers is zero CLUSTERS: near-multiple zeros make 1/((ρ'−ρ)ζ'(ρ')) blow up in correlated fashion. Unconditionally this is the same wall wearing zero-clothing; conditionally it is tamed by explicit gap/moment hypotheses, which is where my partial result draws its honesty line.
obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: The lens's strongest suit: the truncated explicit formula is a pointwise identity valid at the arithmetically synchronized x with total truncation cost O(log³x) at T = x. No exceptional-set-permitting average is used anywhere in the main chain. The only averaging is over zeros, which are the same fixed set for every x — pinning x costs nothing here.

obstacle_positions.parity: Not a sieve argument; μ enters linearly and is dualized to 1/ζ via Perron, so the classical parity wall is not directly binding. But I state plainly where parity re-manifests: unconditional ignorance of the residues 1/ζ'(ρ) IS the parity problem in zero coordinates — the diagonal Σ x^ρ/(ρζ'(ρ)) is M(x) itself. The lens relocates parity; it does not break it.

(2) Numeric killer (a few GPU-days at most): using the first ~2×10^6 zeros, compute D and O_off at the square-sample points X_n ≤ 10^9 already used in calibration; kill if D fails to track −M(x)·log K within the derived error, or if |O_off|/√x drifts upward across the 5.5 decades instead of staying flat near the observed 0.35–0.43 band.
